evidence.description: FIND-009 CONFIRMED-RESOLVED. The prior TWO mutually inconsistent delta mechanisms (a whole-pass 'franklin-trading balance' CLI before/after snapshot vs. an RPC-based sigStatus/usdcDeltaForSig per-signature computation) are no longer both present. The spec now names exactly ONE authoritative mechanism throughout: sol-trade/lib/record-swap.mjs calls solana-verify.mjs::sigStatus(sig) then usdcDeltaForSig(sig, wallet), and 'no franklin-trading balance before/after CLI snapshot is read or relied upon anywhere in this mechanism' (behavioral-spec.md:235-237, repeated verbatim at lines 47-52, 124, 149, 299-303). I grepped every occurrence of 'franklin-trading balance'/'balance.js' across both spec files (18 hits total) and every single one is consistent with 'this feature never calls it' -- zero contradicting occurrences remain.

FIND-009's second, independent complaint -- that the Effectful Shell enumeration for sol-trade/run.sh never mentioned solana-verify.mjs despite PROP-005 requiring it to be mocked -- is also closed: the Effectful Shell bullet for sol-trade/run.sh now explicitly names 'solana-verify.mjs::sigStatus (network RPC, getSignatureStatuses) then solana-verify.mjs::usdcDeltaForSig (network RPC, getTransaction) then node lib/record.mjs' as the exact call sequence inside the new record-swap.mjs. PROP-005's Tool column and the call graph the prose describes are now the SAME call graph.

Cross-checked the spec's claim against the REAL, already-implemented code (Phase 3/gate-3 already ran for this feature per state.json, independent of the invalid 1c gate under review): recordSwap() imports ONLY sigStatus/usdcDeltaForSig from solana-verify.mjs, alreadyRecordedSig from ledger.mjs, and record from lib/record.mjs -- exactly matching the spec's described call graph, mirroring clip-promote/record-payout.mjs verbatim as claimed, and accepting any confirmed delta sign (unlike record-payout.mjs's delta>0 gate) exactly as REQ-002/PROP-007 require. No import of, or call to, any franklin-trading balance subcommand exists anywhere in this file or in skills/earn/sol-trade/run.sh (full file read).

Re-confirmed usdcDeltaForSig sums (post-pre) ONLY over token-balance entries belonging to the ONE passed signature via a single getTransaction RPC call, ignoring every other transfer in the same window -- structurally incapable of the whole-pass-window contamination FIND-009 flagged for the retired balance-CLI mechanism. This module is unmodified by the feature (confirmed no diff from the version iteration-3 already cited).

PROP-005/PROP-007/PROP-016 are exercised exactly as the spec's proof-obligation table describes: a fixture fetchImpl injected directly into recordSwap() for confirmed+positive delta (recorded), confirmed+negative delta (still recorded, net_usdc<0), and both an RPC-status failure and a getTransaction failure (both -> verify-error, never a thrown exception, never a ledger append) -- this is real, already-green evidence that PROP-005's call graph is not merely described but proven.

FIND-010 CONFIRMED-RESOLVED. Re-read the REAL installed package's swap-execution success path directly: the `Signature: ${sig}` line (line 342) is a plain, unwrapped template-string interpolation -- no `chalk.*()` call wraps it anywhere in this function (lines 330-347 read in full) -- confirming the spec's own citation of this exact fact (behavioral-spec.md:40-42) is accurate, not merely self-asserted.

Re-read the REAL installed balance.js in full: `USDC Balance: ${chalk.green(...)}` (line 13) IS chalk-wrapped exactly as the spec claims -- confirming the risk FIND-010 identified was real for that subcommand. The spec's resolution strategy is not to harden a parser against this risk but to eliminate the call to `franklin-trading balance` entirely (no code path in sol-trade/run.sh, record-swap.mjs, or any test in this feature invokes it -- confirmed by reading skills/earn/sol-trade/run.sh in full, which calls only `franklin-trading start`). Eliminating the only chalk-wrapped stdout this feature would otherwise have needed to parse fully closes FIND-010's specific complaint.

The implementation goes further than the spec strictly requires: extractLastSignature() ALSO strips ANSI escape codes (`ANSI_RE = /\x1b\[[0-9;]*m/g`) before regex-matching the Signature line, as defense-in-depth against a hypothetical future chalk-wrapping of that specific line. This is consistent with, and not contradicted by, the spec's PROP-010 ('extractLastSignature is deterministic and total... never throws on malformed/truncated input').

Every REQ-002 EARS clause and Edge Case now traces to a concrete, tool-specified PROP row (PROP-005 through PROP-016), and every PROP's 'Tool' column names an actual, verifiable technique (injectable fetchImpl mirroring an EXISTING proven test file, or a fixture $PATH-stub CLI + fixture-HTTP-RPC-stub bash integration test) rather than a vague aspiration. Cross-checked PROP-005/007/010/012/014/016 against the REAL, already-green test files (skills/earn/sol-trade/lib/__tests__/record-swap.test.mjs, parse-pass.test.mjs, skills/earn/sol-trade/tests/test_run.sh) and found each PROP's described technique is exactly what the real test file does -- the proof obligations are not merely well-formed on paper, they are already satisfied in practice.

FIND-009.note: The spec now defines exactly ONE authoritative delta mechanism (sigStatus -> usdcDeltaForSig via the new record-swap.mjs, mirroring record-payout.mjs), stated consistently across every one of the 18 'franklin-trading balance' mentions in both spec files (zero contradictions found by direct grep), and the Effectful Shell enumeration now explicitly names solana-verify.mjs as PROP-005's Tool column requires. Cross-checked against the REAL, already-implemented skills/earn/sol-trade/lib/record-swap.mjs and its already-green test suite (record-swap.test.mjs) -- the implementation matches the spec's described call graph exactly, with no second/competing mechanism anywhere in the actual codebase either.

FIND-010.note: The spec eliminates the only chalk/ANSI-wrapped stdout this feature would otherwise have needed to parse (franklin-trading balance's USDC Balance line, dist/commands/balance.js:13, re-confirmed chalk-wrapped in the real installed package) by never calling that subcommand anywhere in the feature (confirmed against the real sol-trade/run.sh, which calls only `franklin-trading start`). The Signature: line it DOES parse is re-confirmed plain-text/unwrapped in the real installed jupiter.js:342. The implementation additionally strips ANSI codes defensively in parse-pass.mjs (belt-and-suspenders, not spec-mandated) -- see FIND-011 for a minor, non-blocking gap in that defensive path's own test coverage.
